We use a variation of the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1\,⟹\,{cos}^{2}⁡x=1-{sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we rewrite the denominator and calculate the resulting integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int (\frac{1}{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\cdot \frac{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x})\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡x}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{{cos}^{2}⁡x})\text{d}x \\  & =\int ({sec}^{2}⁡x+\operatorname{sec}⁡x\operatorname{tan}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡x+\operatorname{sec}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
